title: WPSS/1897/2022 of VINOD KUMAR Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
ON THE 11TH DAY OF OCTOBER, 2022
BEFORE:
HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE MANOJ KUMAR TIWARI
WRIT PETITION (S/S) No. 1897 OF 2022
BETWEEN:
Vinod Kumar .... Petitioner
(By Mr. Dushyant Mainali, Advocate)
AND:
State of Uttarakhand & others ... Respondents
(By Mr. P.S. Bisht, learned Additional C.S.C.)
JUDGMENT
1. Fresh affidavit filed by petitioner in support of
writ petition is taken on record. Consequently,
miscellaneous application (IA No. 2 of 2022) stands
disposed of.
2. Petitioner was appointed against Group-D post
of Chowkidar in Ayurvedic Department w.e.f.
20.04.1986. At the time of appointment, his date of
birth was recorded as 01.02.1965 in his service book. As
per the said date of birth, petitioner would complete age
of superannuation on 31.01.2025.
3. In this writ petition, petitioner has sought the
following relief:-
(i) Issue a writ order or direction in the nature of
mandamus commanding and directing the
respondents to correct the date of birth of the
petitioner as 01.02.1968 in place of wrongly
mentioned date of birth as 01.02.1965 in the service
records of the petitioner including the online service
records.

2
(ii) Issue a writ order or direction in the nature of
mandamus commanding and directing the
respondents to provide all the service benefits to the
petitioner attach to his post considering his date of
birth 01.02.1968 as his correct date of birth.
4. According to petitioner, his date of birth was
wrongly recorded as 01.02.1965 which should have
been recorded as 01.02.1968. In support of this
contention, learned counsel for the petitioner has
referred to a 'School Leaving Certificate' issued by Head
Master, Junior High School, Tanda Badli, District Rampur
(U.P.). Reliance has also been placed on High School
Marksheet issued to petitioner on 27.06.1990. In both
these documents, petitioner's date of birth is recorded
as 01.02.1968.
5. Learned State Counsel, however, contends
that as per Statutory Rules governing the field, date of
birth as recorded in the service book at the time of
appointment to a post under the State, is final and no
request for change of date of birth can thereafter be
entertained. He further submits that Hon'ble Supreme
Court has repeatedly held that request for correction of
date of birth, at the fag end of service career, cannot be
entertained. He points out that High School qualification
was acquired by petitioner four years after his
appointment in the department, therefore, the date of
birth as recorded in High School Mark-sheet, cannot be
relied upon for seeking correction of date of birth in his
service record.
6. This Court finds substance in the contention
made by learned State Counsel. Hon'ble Supreme Court
in the case of State of Uttarakhand vs. Pitamber
Dutt Semwal (2005)11SCC 477 has held that request

3
for correction of date of birth by a Government Servant
cannot be entertained at the fag end of service career.
In the case of Karnataka Rural Infrastructure
Development Ltd. vs. T.P. Nataraja & others,
reported in 2021 SCC Online SC 767 Hon'ble Supreme
Court has summarised the law regarding change of date
of birth in para 10 the said judgment, which is extracted
below:-
"10. Considering the aforesaid decisions of this Court
the law on change of date of birth can be summarized
as under:
(i) application for change of date of birth can only
be as per the relevant provisions/regulations
applicable;
(ii) even if there is cogent evidence, the same
cannot be claimed as a matter of right;
(iii) application can be rejected on the ground of
delay and latches also more particularly when
it is made at the fag end of service and/or
when the employee is about to retire on
attaining the age of superannuation."
7. In the present case, if petitioner's date of birth
was wrongly recorded at the time of his appointment, it
was incumbent upon him to make request for correction
thereof at the relevant point of time. After appointment,
service book of every Government Servant is prepared
in which he is required to put his signature on the page
in which date of birth is also recorded, in
acknowledgment of the fact that he has checked the
entries made in the service book.
8. It is not the case of petitioner that his date of
birth was changed by interpolation after preparation of
service book. As per provision contained in Rule 2 of
Uttarakhand Recruitment to Service (Determination of
Date of Birth) Rules, 2003, the date of birth, as recorded
in the service book, cannot be altered. English
translation of the relevant provision is quoted below:-

4
"2. Determination of correct date of birth or
age. - The date of birth of a Government servant as
recorded in the certificate of his having passed the
High School or equivalent examination at the time of
his entry into the Government service or where a
Government servant has not passed any such
examinations aforesaid or has passed such
examination after joining the service, the date of
birth or the age recorded in his service book at the
time of his entry into the Government service shall
be deemed to be his correct date of birth or age, as
the case may be, for all purposes in relation of his
service, including eligibility for promotion,
superannuation, premature retirement or retirement
benefits, and no application or representation shall
be entertained for correction of such date of age in
any circumstances whatsoever."
9. Learned counsel for the petitioner then
submitted that a committee was constituted to consider
similar request by certain employees of Ayurvedic
Department for correction of their date of birth and
Chairman of the committee issued a letter to the
Principal, Junior High School, Tanda Badli, Rampur to
certify petitioner's mark sheet and transfer certificate,
so that his date of birth be corrected in service record.
Learned counsel submitted that similar order was passed
by Chairman of the Committee in respect of other
employees also, who had raised grievance regarding
their date of birth.
10. Since the Statute governing the field does not
permit correction of date of birth at the fag end of
service career, therefore, this Court has no hesitation in
holding that letter dated 26.04.2019 issued by District
Ayurvedic and Unani Officer, Pithoragarh is without any
authority of law. The said letter appears to have been
issued by respondent no. 3 in ignorance of Statute,
therefore, the Secretary, Department of Personnel,
State of Uttarakhand, Dehradun is directed to issue
necessary instructions to all Head of Department/Head

5
of Office to make them aware of the statutory provisions
dealing with correction/change in date of birth as
recorded in service book of Government Servants.
11. For the facts and reasons mentioned in the
foregoing paragraphs of this judgment, the relief, as
claimed by the petitioner, cannot be granted.
12. Accordingly, writ petition fails and is hereby
dismissed.
13. Registry shall communicate this order to
Secretary, Personnel and Appointment, Government of
Uttarakhand, Dehradun, on or before 15.10.2022.
(MANOJ KUMAR TIWARI, J.)
Aswal
